sections.title: Understanding Linux
sections.coverage: Explain Linux, distributions, common uses, and the relationship between the kernel, shell, and applications. Introduce the system before manipulating it.

sections.title: Understanding the Learning Environment
sections.coverage: Introduce the learner environment, host versus lab boundaries, supported setup guidance, and safe recovery habits. Exact platforms will be selected during implementation. Establish safe boundaries before commands change state.

sections.title: Getting Comfortable with the Terminal
sections.coverage: Introduce the terminal, shell prompt, command structure, arguments, and basic interaction. Provide the interface used throughout the story.

sections.title: Navigating the Filesystem
sections.coverage: Explain the working directory, filesystem hierarchy, absolute and relative paths, and movement between directories. Locate team resources through that interface.

sections.title: Finding Help and Documentation
sections.coverage: Show how to discover command usage and interpret help, manuals, and relevant documentation. Enable independent discovery once navigation is familiar.

sections.title: Inspecting the System
sections.coverage: Introduce environment identity, basic system information, and the distinction between ordinary and privileged operations. Use navigation and help to identify the system.

sections.title: Building Safe Command-Line Habits
sections.coverage: Bring together command reading, history, careful verification, error interpretation, and responsible use of the lab. Consolidate safe habits before working with team files.

courses.title: Files, Text Processing, and the Shell

sections.title: Creating and Managing Files
sections.coverage: Cover creating, copying, moving, renaming, and removing files and directories using disposable sample data. Create the working data for the story.

sections.title: Reading and Editing Text
sections.coverage: Cover inspecting text files, working with a text editor, and making understandable changes to sample configuration files. Make the working data readable and editable.

sections.title: Finding Files and Searching Content
sections.coverage: Explain file discovery, content searching, and selecting relevant results from directory trees and text. Locate relevant material before processing it.

sections.title: Filtering and Transforming Text
sections.coverage: Introduce selecting fields, sorting, counting, comparing, and transforming structured sample text. Turn located material into useful summaries.

sections.title: Streams and Redirection
sections.coverage: Explain standard input, output, errors, and controlling where command data flows. Explain data flow before combining commands.

sections.title: Combining Commands with Pipelines
sections.coverage: Show how commands cooperate in pipelines, how to inspect intermediate results, and how to recognize failures. Combine earlier transformations into workflows.

sections.title: Archives and Compression
sections.coverage: Cover packaging, inspecting, extracting, and verifying archives without confusing an archive with a complete backup strategy. Package the files and results for later transfer and recovery.

sections.title: Linux Identities and Privilege
sections.coverage: Explain users, identity contexts, administrative privilege, and why access boundaries matter. Establish who is acting on the team system.

sections.title: Managing Users
sections.coverage: Introduce user accounts, account information, and responsible account lifecycle changes in the lab. Give team members distinct identities.

sections.title: Managing Groups
sections.coverage: Explain group membership and using groups to organize shared access. Organize those identities for shared work.

sections.title: Understanding File Permissions
sections.coverage: Explain ownership and interpreting file and directory permission behavior. Explain access rules before changing them.

sections.title: Changing Ownership and Access
sections.coverage: Show deliberate ownership and permission changes with verification and least-privilege reasoning. Apply those rules to the shared files.

sections.title: Managing Privileged Operations
sections.coverage: Explain controlled elevation, the impact of administrative commands, and avoiding unnecessary privilege. Bound administrative changes to the system.

sections.title: Reviewing Access and Basic Security
sections.coverage: Combine account, group, permission, and privilege knowledge to identify common access mistakes and improve a sample system. Combine identity and file knowledge into access review.

sections.title: Understanding Software Sources
sections.coverage: Explain packages, repositories, dependencies, and trusted software sources while noting distribution differences. Establish trust before installing team software.

sections.title: Installing and Maintaining Software
sections.coverage: Cover inspecting, installing, updating, and removing approved lab software with state verification. Manage software from those sources.

sections.title: Understanding Processes
sections.coverage: Explain process identity, relationships, execution state, and how running programs appear to system tools. Observe the programs installed earlier as running work.

sections.title: Controlling Processes
sections.coverage: Cover foreground and background work, job control, signals, and responsible process termination. Control that work deliberately.

sections.title: Inspecting System Resources
sections.coverage: Introduce CPU, memory, and resource observations and distinguishing evidence from assumptions about performance. Inspect the resources used by running work.

sections.title: Managing Services
sections.coverage: Explain service lifecycle, startup behavior, configuration changes, and checking actual service behavior in the supported environment. Organize long-running work as managed services.

sections.title: Reading Logs and Diagnosing Operational Problems
sections.coverage: Show how to connect symptoms, service state, resource observations, and log evidence when investigating common failures. Use logs to explain the behavior of those services.

sections.title: Networking Fundamentals
sections.coverage: Introduce addresses, interfaces, routes, ports, and the basic path between communicating systems. Explain how the team reaches the system.

sections.title: Name Resolution and Connectivity
sections.coverage: Explain name lookup and a systematic approach to checking connectivity and locating the failing stage. Locate connectivity failures before adding remote sessions.

sections.title: Authorized Remote Access
sections.coverage: Introduce remote sessions, authentication, host verification, and responsible connections between authorized lab endpoints. Use known network paths for authorized access.

sections.title: Remote File Transfer
sections.coverage: Cover moving sample files between authorized systems and verifying transfer results. Move the team files over those connections.

sections.title: Understanding Storage and Filesystems
sections.coverage: Explain storage devices, partitions at a conceptual level, filesystems, capacity, and usage inspection. Explain where transferred data resides.

sections.title: Mounts and Disposable Storage
sections.coverage: Show mount behavior and storage changes only within disposable lab resources, including recovery and cleanup. Attach disposable storage after understanding its role.

sections.title: Backing Up Sample Data
sections.coverage: Explain backup scope, destination choices, integrity checks, and producing recoverable copies of sample data. Preserve copies of the stored team data.

sections.title: Restoring Data and Resolving Storage Problems
sections.coverage: Cover verified restoration and evidence-based diagnosis of bounded capacity, mount, and access failures. Complete preservation by demonstrating restoration.

sections.title: From Commands to Scripts
sections.coverage: Introduce script structure, execution, readability, and turning an understood manual workflow into a script. Automate an operation already understood manually.

sections.title: Variables, Parameters, and Quoting
sections.coverage: Explain passing data into scripts and handling spaces, empty values, and special characters deliberately. Make the operation accept changing team inputs.

sections.title: Conditions and Decisions
sections.coverage: Cover conditions and branching based on input, file state, and command outcomes. Respond to different input and system states.

sections.title: Loops and Repeated Work
sections.coverage: Explain iteration over appropriate inputs while preserving correct handling of filenames and failure cases. Repeat the operation across relevant inputs.

sections.title: Functions and Reuse
sections.coverage: Introduce small functions, clear responsibilities, and organizing scripts without unnecessary complexity. Organize repeated script behavior for reuse.

sections.title: Errors, Debugging, and Logging
sections.coverage: Cover input validation, exit behavior, useful diagnostics, and debugging normal and failure paths. Make failures visible before relying on automation.

sections.title: Automating Routine Administration
sections.coverage: Combine scripting skills in repeatable reporting or sample-backup workflows, with scheduling concepts, visible results, and safe reruns. Combine earlier script features into routine operations.

sections.title: A Structured Troubleshooting Method
sections.coverage: Explain symptoms, scope, hypotheses, evidence collection, controlled changes, and verification. Establish a common method before diagnosing incidents.

sections.title: Diagnosing Access Problems
sections.coverage: Revisit identities, groups, permissions, and remote access through coherent access-failure demonstrations. Revisit team access using the diagnostic method.

sections.title: Diagnosing Process and Service Failures
sections.coverage: Combine process state, service behavior, configuration, resource use, and logs to investigate operational failures. Apply the same method to running software.

sections.title: Diagnosing Network Problems
sections.coverage: Apply layered reasoning to addressing, routing, name resolution, ports, and authorized remote connectivity. Extend diagnosis to remote communication.

sections.title: Diagnosing Storage and Recovery Problems
sections.coverage: Bring together capacity, mounts, permissions, backups, and verified sample-data restoration. Extend diagnosis to stored data and recovery.

sections.title: Reviewing Security and Operational Health
sections.coverage: Combine least privilege, software maintenance, access review, exposure awareness, and evidence-based system checks. Combine findings into a broader operational review.

sections.title: End-to-End Administration and Handoff
sections.coverage: Demonstrate an integrated system workflow, routine automation, a bounded incident, recovery verification, and clear operational documentation. Connect the entire story through recovery and handoff.
